protocol_versions._description: HART protocol revision history and security implications

5.name: HART 5
features: Long frame format with Unique Identifier
vulnerabilities: No encryption - all traffic in cleartext
No authentication - any master can send commands

6.name: HART 6
features: Long Tag support (32 chars ISO Latin 1)
vulnerabilities: No encryption - all traffic in cleartext
Device lock can be bypassed with master reset
Extended address space increases attack surface

security_checks._description: Security assessment criteria by protocol version

checks.name: Legacy Protocol Version
checks.description: Device uses HART revision 5 or earlier with no security features
checks.recommendation: Upgrade to HART 7 devices with WirelessHART security or implement network-level protection

checks.name: No Write Protection
checks.description: Device accepts write commands without authentication
checks.recommendation: Enable write protection mode or implement physical access controls

checks.name: Unencrypted HART-IP
checks.recommendation: Use VPN or TLS tunneling for HART-IP traffic

checks.name: Master Reset Available
checks.recommendation: Restrict physical access; monitor for reset commands

checks.name: Poll Address Writable
checks.recommendation: Can be used to cause device conflicts on multidrop networks

checks.name: Configuration Change Counter Not Monitored
checks.recommendation: Implement configuration change monitoring via Command 0/38
